Mutations can occur, but that does not refute the findings that twins have a low coincidence on being homosexual. You would have to show that the genetic mutation occurred in a specific location(s) in all cases of discordant twins.

In fact that would be a great way to help locate the "Gay gene" which has alluded scientists thus far.
Since the rate of mutation is pretty low, you'd expect the effects of the mutations to be similarly uncommon.

Just to add to this, there are also differences due to cytoplasmic inheritance (asymmetry of distribution of proteins at the point the zygote splits), and other epigenetic factors resulting from different developmental environments.

We can go on and on listing possible variances in the developmental period, but it's a huge leap of faith to say that that list fully explains why 85% of identical homosexual twins do not share sexual preferences. It's a much more simple answer to say that homosexuals are not born that way.
